nonBlockingObservations.observation: The r3 response row still says in the present tense that §5.1's budget uses the larger of the concurrent summed high-water and the per-process counters. Section 5.2's column is still "Peak process-tree RSS". Section 5.1 now says the exploratory figure is cgroupMemoryPeak and is never labelled RSS. A shared page is charged to the cgroup once and counted in every process RSS that maps it, so cgroupMemoryPeak can be below that column. D4 still revisits the targets after the first exploratory measurement, and qualification stays on D13.

Kernel memory.peak is the max for the cgroup and its descendants since cgroup creation, or since the last reset on that same file descriptor. A write resets later reads on that descriptor only. The plan calls this the run's figure and does not say the cgroup is created for the run or that one descriptor is reset at run start. A later read of a cgroup that outlives the run is cumulative. The file exists on non-root cgroups; a missing file is not given the incomplete outcome macOS has.

"Four design rounds (M3-Q0 r2–r8)" is not a count those review requests enumerate. r2–r6 iterate the taskstats/event-channel join, r7 was not reviewed, and r8 replaces that mechanism with ptrace and is still REQUIRED-FINDINGS. The claim that each reviewed per-process attempt still had loss or attribution gaps matches those verdicts. r8 does not itself select memory.peak.
